s12.title: Most Common Issues Seen 2025
s12.publisher: Chief Delphi, opening post by the mentor of Team 254's CheesyCare group

bet.text: Spend no time lining up: the End Effector's "Flying V" wedge aligns it to the tip of the Reef pipe.

demand.text: Win matches with efficient coral scoring, focused on L3 and L4, that is resilient to defense. Collect ranking points with three or more coral in auto and a deep cage climb, and score algae in the processor to help coopertition.

auto.text: The driver picks a scoring sequence. A* and AD* generate paths around obstacles in real time, and common feeder-to-branch paths are cached when the robot initializes.
A reply that reads as the team's says caching saved over 100 ms per path and was needed for five pieces.

cycle.text: Take coral from the floor Intake or the Funnel; the Indexer aligns it into the End Effector. The Elevator goes to level, auto align brings the robot in, the Flying V finds the pipe, and a beam break that detects the pipe triggers the release.

endgame.text: The roller claw deploys, its powered wheels grab the deep cage into a latch, and a winch pivots the claw to pull the robot under the cage and off the ground.

fallback.text: The Funnel takes coral from the Coral Station if the Intake breaks.
A reply that reads as the team's says it was used a lot at Sacramento and East Bay, and kept as a failsafe though unlikely to be needed at the championship.

gave_up.text: A post that reads as the team's says the robot placed coral with its drivetrain, so it could not strafe in: lateral and heading error had to be within tolerance first, and near the reef it had to back up.
The team called its L1 as good as anyone's but scorable only opposite the ground intake, and wanted more climber space and power.

changed.text: A one-week AlphaBot showed that an end effector without alignment compliance sometimes drops coral. L1 scoring was removed on practice day of the first event because it was not working, and stayed off for that event.
After the season, a post that reads as the team's said it would choose a more traditional end effector, since aligning to the pipe proved much easier than expected.

outcome.text: 42-7-0 in official play; finalist in the Milstein division; ranked 10 of the pooled top 20 (OPR 106.58, Milstein).

solves.text: Accelerate hard on short cycles and resist tipping

Square frame side
3x1 tubes put the bellypan above the floor by
Motors on the robot

solves.text: Pick up coral from the floor in any orientation without jamming

cost.text: The binder says the deploy gear drives a 4-bar linkage; a reply that reads as the team's says the intake was not a 4-bar, took more force from front and side impacts, and broke a couple of times at the regionals

facts.text: Deploys in about
Roller surface speed, about
Rollers are rubber tubing over foam, for smooth, light, continuous surfaces
The front roller floats on a sprung plate: it opens for long-ways coral and collapses against a wall
Rubber bands act as flat belts that pull coral through dead spots

solves.text: Take coral directly from the Coral Station in autonomous, or if the Intake breaks

Steep angle for greater funneling speed
1/32 in polycarbonate stiffened by edge bends and carbon fiber rods

solves.text: Reorient coral from two sources and align it for handoff to the End Effector

facts.text: Eight 4 in flex and star wheels, with cut rims and spokes to prevent jams
Wheel surface speed, about
Two beam breaks, front and rear, inform the state machine

solves.text: Lift the End Effector to all four reef levels and the Barge, stiff enough to place accurately

facts.text: Travel, about
Full travel in about
Two Kraken X60s; 9 mm belts run inside the tubes
A welded A-frame stabilizes it and mounts the Climber

functions.name: End Effector

solves.text: Place coral without missing or stopping to line up, and handle algae with the same mechanism

cost.text: A post that reads as the team's says the design added many constraints (handoff, L1, sensing, not de-scoring, algae, weight), with issues still being fought in the Milstein playoffs

functions.type: wristed flex-wheel scorer with a Flying V

facts.text: Wrist rotation
Wrist rotates in about
Coral wheel surface speed, about
Beam breaks position the coral and detect the pipe, which triggers the release
A sprung hoop lets coral pass through for L1 and becomes a hardstop during handoff
A stealth wheel and grippy studs grab algae, on the motor shared with coral

functions.name: Climber

solves.text: Align to the deep cage and climb it quickly

cost.text: The team says brushing bumpers against an unclimbed partner could lose the climb, and wishes it climbed higher

functions.type: roller claw with latch and winch

facts.text: Two 4 in flex wheels grab the vertical pipe of the cage
A 30 lbf gas spring deploys the claw
The winch sits on the bellypan for a lower center of gravity; gearbox 1:224 on a Kraken X60
A ratchet and pawl holds the robot up after the match

functions.name: Localization

solves.text: Know the robot's position for auto-align scoring and obstacle avoidance

functions.type: Limelight AprilTag vision with swerve odometry

facts.text: Two Limelight 4s give a MegaTag 1 pose near tags; farther away odometry leads, with periodic vision corrections
A reply that reads as the team's says it used MegaTag 1 range with gyro bearing unless it saw several tags or was very close, and only the tag on the scoring face when scoring
The AlphaBot showed cameras must be set back from the corners to see tags near the reef

solves.text: Drive optimized, collision-free paths in autonomous

facts.text: Pre-computed paths are merged with on-the-fly paths
A reply that reads as the team's says PID control acted about the held coral instead of the robot's center, because that is the point that matters
The same reply says robot-relative tracking gave cross-track error its own gain, since it was the less forgiving error at the peg

functions.name: Tele-op state machine

solves.text: Let a single driver run every mechanism

functions.type: centralized state machine with driver modes

facts.text: The driver selects coral, manual coral, or algae and climb modes; presets move the Elevator and End Effector together
The published code tracks coral in six states from the indexer and claw sensors, and resets to none when a wait times out

decisions.choice: Passive alignment in the End Effector
decisions.because: it removes time spent lining up and dropped coral
decisions.instead_of: an end effector without alignment compliance, tried on the AlphaBot

decisions.choice: Drive into the reef to score
decisions.because: a scoring motion that coordinates elevator and arm is slower
decisions.instead_of: a pivoting arm, tried on the AlphaBot

decisions.choice: Lift algae and shoot it lightly into the Barge
decisions.because: the team wanted never to miss
the wheel is 2 in wide and grippier, and the azimuth runs on a gear
decisions.instead_of: the SDS MK4i modules of previous years, with a belt azimuth

decisions.choice: Intake on the side opposite scoring
decisions.because: it minimizes the distance and rotations needed

decisions.choice: Keep a Funnel beside the floor Intake
decisions.because: it is an alternate path for autonomous and redundancy if the Intake breaks

decisions.choice: Remove L1 scoring at the first event
decisions.because: it was not working, and the robot did better than if the team had kept solving it live

decisions.choice: Build an AlphaBot in one week on the 2023 elevator and drivebase
decisions.because: the team wanted to learn gameplay early and give software a robot to develop on

decisions.choice: Cache paths when the robot initializes
decisions.because: it saved over 100 ms per path in autonomous, needed for five pieces (from a reply that reads as the team's)
